components.text: Water constantly moves between Earth's surface and the atmosphere in an endless cycle. Understanding this process is key to comprehending weather, climate, and environmental systems.

components.title: Understanding the Water Cycle
components.dek: How water transforms and travels through our planet
components.hook: Water doesn't stay in one place—it's constantly evaporating, condensing, and falling as precipitation in a continuous planetary process.
components.model: Think of it as nature's recycling system, where water changes form but never disappears.
components.model_note: This cycle has been running for billions of years.
components.closing_note: Every water molecule on Earth has cycled through this process countless times over billions of years.

components.title: Evaporation
components.body: Water from oceans, lakes, and rivers is heated by the sun and transforms into water vapor, rising into the atmosphere. This is the cycle's starting point.
components.takeaway: Heat + water = water vapor in the air

components.title: Condensation
components.body: As water vapor rises and cools in the upper atmosphere, it condenses into tiny water droplets. These droplets cluster together to form clouds.
components.takeaway: Cool air + water vapor = liquid water droplets

components.title: Precipitation
components.body: When water droplets in clouds become heavy enough, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This returns water to the surface.
components.takeaway: Heavy clouds + gravity = water returns to Earth

components.title: The Complete Cycle in Action
components.body: Imagine a raindrop that falls on a mountain lake. Solar radiation heats it until it becomes water vapor and rises into the sky. As it climbs higher and encounters cooler air at 10,000 feet, it condenses into a cloud droplet. More droplets join it, and eventually the cloud becomes so saturated that the droplet falls as rain on a forest far away. It soaks into the soil, is absorbed by tree roots, and transpired back into the air through leaves. The cycle continues endlessly.
components.code:
Solar Input → Evaporation → Rising Vapor → Cooling
     → Condensation → Cloud Formation → Precipitation
     → Collection → Transpiration → Back to Start
components.code_caption: The water cycle continuously repeats this sequence.

questions.question: What is the primary energy source that drives the water cycle?
questions.explanation: The sun's heat is the primary driver—it provides the energy needed to evaporate water from Earth's surface into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which process describes water vapor turning into liquid water droplets?
questions.explanation: Condensation is the phase change from gas (water vapor) to liquid. This occurs when water vapor cools in the upper atmosphere.

questions.question: What happens to water after it falls as precipitation?
options: It flows to the ocean, infiltrates soil, or is absorbed by plants
questions.explanation: Precipitation can follow multiple pathways: it may run off into rivers and oceans, soak into groundwater, or be absorbed by plants and eventually transpired back to the atmosphere.

objectives: Explain the three main stages of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, and precipitation
Identify the sun's role as the primary energy source driving the water cycle
Describe the pathways water takes after precipitation falls to Earth
Understand how water continuously cycles through different forms and locations
